new_nodes.name: Multi-agent RL & centralized training, decentralized execution
new_nodes.authors: Ryan Lowe · Yi Wu · Aviv Tamar · Jean Harb · Pieter Abbeel · Igor Mordatch; Chao Yu · Akash Velu · Eugene Vinitsky et al.
new_nodes.text: Several learners act in a shared environment, so each agent's environment includes the others' changing policies. Centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) trains with shared information and acts on local observations.
new_nodes.handle: MADDPG trains each agent with a critic that sees all agents' actions, while actors use only local observations ([Lowe et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02275)). MAPPO, which is PPO with a centralized value function, was competitive with or better than off-policy baselines on particle worlds, SMAC, Google Research Football and Hanabi with little tuning ([Yu et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01955)).
new_nodes.boundary: Single-agent guarantees do not carry over. Other learners make the environment non-stationary ([Lowe et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.02275)), and exact finite-horizon decentralized planning is NEXP-complete even for two agents ([Bernstein et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.3836)). Return against training partners does not show behaviour with new partners ([Lanctot et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00832)).
new_nodes.test: Train several seeds, then cross-play agents from different runs and against held-out partners. Report the self-play versus cross-play return gap alongside constraint violations.

new_nodes.name: Game-theoretic equilibria & population training
new_nodes.authors: Yoav Shoham · Kevin Leyton-Brown; Marc Lanctot · Vinicius Zambaldi · Audrunas Gruslys et al.
new_nodes.text: A solution concept, such as Nash or correlated equilibrium, defines which joint policy counts as stable when each agent optimizes its own payoff. Population methods approximate one through repeated best responses.
new_nodes.handle: At a Nash equilibrium no player gains by deviating alone. Finding a sample Nash equilibrium of a general-sum finite game is PPAD-complete, while correlated equilibria can be computed by linear programming ([Shoham and Leyton-Brown](http://www.masfoundations.org/)). PSRO trains approximate best responses to mixtures of earlier policies and picks meta-strategies by empirical game-theoretic analysis ([Lanctot et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00832)).
new_nodes.boundary: An equilibrium is stable, not necessarily good. It need not maximize welfare or match the principal's intent, and general-sum games can have many equilibria. Empirical game analysis covers only the policies in the population ([Lanctot et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00832)).
new_nodes.test: Measure exploitability, the best-response gain against the trained population, and compare welfare at the equilibrium found with the cooperative optimum.

new_nodes.name: Multi-agent evaluation with held-out co-players
new_nodes.authors: Joel Z. Leibo · Edgar Duéñez-Guzmán · Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets et al.; Allan Dafoe · Edward Hughes · Yoram Bachrach et al.
new_nodes.text: Score agents by how they perform alongside co-players they never trained with, in cooperative, competitive and mixed-motive scenarios.
new_nodes.handle: Melting Pot pairs a substrate with a pre-trained background population used only for evaluation. Its 80+ scenarios include social dilemmas, reciprocity and resource sharing, and it reveals weaknesses that training performance hides ([Leibo et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.06857)). Cooperative AI treats such joint-welfare problems as a research target ([Dafoe et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.08630)).
new_nodes.boundary: Generalization is measured only against the background populations that were built. Real counterparties, humans and markets of LLM agents are not covered, and a scenario score is not a welfare guarantee. [Scope](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.06857)
new_nodes.test: Hold out co-player populations, and for LLM agents hold out counterpart models and prompts. Report focal return and group welfare per scenario, with uncertainty over seeds and co-players.

new_nodes.name: Multi-agent LLM systems & failure modes
new_nodes.authors: Mert Cemri · Melissa Z. Pan · Shuyi Yang et al.; Yilun Du · Shuang Li · Antonio Torralba · Joshua B. Tenenbaum · Igor Mordatch; Andries Smit et al.
new_nodes.text: Several role-assigned LLM agents exchange messages to plan, critique, debate or split a task. Gains over a single agent are not automatic, and new failures arise between agents.
new_nodes.handle: Multiagent debate improved reported math, strategy and factuality scores ([Du et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14325)). MAST sorts 1,600+ annotated traces from 7 frameworks into 14 failure modes in three categories, validated with kappa = 0.88: system design, inter-agent misalignment and task verification ([Cemri et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657)).
new_nodes.boundary: Multi-agent systems often gain little on benchmarks ([Cemri et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657)). In one comparison, untuned debate did not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling ([Smit et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17371)). These protocols carry no equilibrium or correctness guarantee.
new_nodes.test: Compare against a single agent and self-consistency at matched tokens. Tag failed traces by MAST category with a human-audited judge, then inject one faulty or compromised agent and measure how far the fault propagates.

new_nodes.name: Agent-to-agent prompt-injection propagation
new_nodes.authors: Stav Cohen · Ron Bitton · Ben Nassi; Donghyun Lee · Mo Tiwari
new_nodes.text: A self-replicating prompt makes each compromised assistant or agent pass the injection to the next, through shared retrieval stores or inter-agent messages.
new_nodes.handle: Morris II chains indirect injections through RAG-connected email assistants and extracts data across hops ([Cohen et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02817)). Prompt Infection spreads from one LLM to the next inside multi-agent systems, even when agents do not share all communications ([Lee and Tiwari](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07283)).
new_nodes.boundary: These are researcher-built testbeds. Neither LLM Tagging nor traditional defenses alone stop propagation, and how often this happens in deployed agent networks has not been measured ([Lee and Tiwari](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07283)).
new_nodes.test: Seed one agent with a self-replicating payload. Measure hop count, the fraction of agents compromised and the data exfiltrated, with and without message tagging and capability-scoped tools.

new_edges.text: SLT extended to RL: the concentration of a generalized posterior over policies is governed by the LLC of the regret function. In one gridworld, SGD training moves through stages where regret drops sharply while λ̂ rises. Theory plus a single-environment test; transfer to closed-loop control utility is untested.

Preference-data concept analysis flagged physics-query sycophancy that DPO on Dolci amplifies in Llama-3.1-8B. The best training intervention reduced it on average, but recovery was partial and not statistically reliable; only link hallucination recovered reliably.

new_edges.relation: a grader used as a reward is overoptimized
new_edges.text: Measure with a judge; optimize against it and Goodhart applies. In a synthetic-gold setup, gold reward-model score follows a different functional form under RL and under best-of-n optimization against a proxy reward model, and too much optimization hurts gold performance. Keep an independent grader held out whenever a judge becomes a reward.

new_edges.relation: calibrate judges against humans and abstain when unsure
new_edges.text: Selective evaluation trusts a judge only when its calibrated confidence clears a threshold and escalates otherwise, giving a provable human-agreement level: over 80% agreement at almost 80% coverage on a Chatbot Arena subset where GPT-4 alone almost never reaches 80%.

RLAIF trains the reward model on LLM-labeled preferences and matched RLHF on summarization and dialogue tasks. Use it when human labels are the bottleneck; the reward then inherits the judge's biases.

new_edges.relation: executable checks as training signal, on held-out repositories
new_edges.text: SWE-Gym's 2,438 tasks with executable unit tests supply a test-passing reward for rejection-sampling fine-tuning, giving up to 19% absolute gains on SWE-bench. Its repositories are kept separate from SWE-bench's to avoid contamination: train on one environment, report on another.

pass^k, the chance that all k i.i.d. trials succeed averaged over tasks, has an unbiased estimate E_task[C(c,k)/C(n,k)] from n trials with c successes. Report it with uncertainty over tasks, the sampling unit, rather than single-trial pass rates.

A pre-deployment score estimates risk on a fixed task distribution. Deployed models meet shifts, some benign and some harmful, so track risk sequentially as labels arrive and intervene only on harmful shift.

Article 72 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to run a post-market monitoring system that actively and systematically collects, documents and analyses performance data throughout the system's lifetime.

new_edges.relation: other learners make the environment non-stationary
new_edges.text: Q-learning faces non-stationarity and policy-gradient variance grows with the number of agents; MADDPG's centralized critics condition on other agents' actions during training, while execution stays decentralized.

new_edges.relation: PPO with a centralized value function
new_edges.text: MAPPO achieved competitive or superior results to off-policy methods on particle worlds, SMAC, Google Research Football and Hanabi with minimal tuning, in cooperative settings.

new_edges.relation: decentralized POMDPs are harder than POMDPs
new_edges.text: Finite-horizon decentralized MDPs and POMDPs are NEXP-complete even for small numbers of agents, so decentralized planning does not reduce to centralized belief-state planning.

new_edges.relation: best responses to populations rather than to one partner
new_edges.text: Independent RL can overfit to co-trained partners, measured by joint-policy correlation; PSRO trains best responses to policy mixtures and generalizes independent RL, iterated best response, double oracle and fictitious play.
CIRL is a cooperative, partial-information game between human and robot in which both are rewarded by the human's reward function and only the human knows it initially.

Debate trains agents by self-play on a zero-sum game judged by a human. By complexity-theoretic analogy, optimal play answers PSPACE questions with polynomial-time judges, but whether real debates reach that play is empirical.

With two expert LLMs debating, non-expert judges reached 76% accuracy (models) and 88% (humans), against 48% and 60% naive baselines, on information-asymmetric reading-comprehension questions. Making debaters more persuasive improved judge accuracy.

new_edges.relation: benchmark multi-agent systems against single-agent baselines
new_edges.text: Multi-agent LLM systems often gain little on popular benchmarks; MAST's task-verification failures mean end-state checks and matched-compute single-agent baselines are needed before adding agents.

new_edges.relation: a judge validated against human annotation
new_edges.text: MAST scales failure annotation with an LLM-as-a-judge pipeline after checking its agreement with expert human annotations, the calibration step a judge needs before it replaces humans.
Melting Pot tests MARL agents against background populations used only for evaluation, revealing weaknesses not apparent from training performance alone.

new_edges.relation: held-out counterpart agents for LLM systems
new_edges.text: Proposed: evaluate multi-agent LLM systems with held-out counterpart models and prompts, as Melting Pot holds out co-players. Single-environment pass^k does not test robustness to new partners.
An adversarial self-replicating prompt triggers a cascade of indirect injections across RAG-connected assistants, each compromising the retrieval store of the next.
Prompt Infection propagates between agents even when they do not share all communications. LLM Tagging combined with existing safeguards mitigated spread, but neither alone sufficed.

new_edges.relation: treat other agents' messages as untrusted data
new_edges.text: Proposed: apply CaMeL-style control/data-flow separation to inter-agent messages, so a compromised agent's output cannot choose another agent's tool calls. CaMeL is evaluated on single-agent AgentDojo, not on multi-agent pipelines.

The Virtual Donkey guardrail detected Morris II propagation with a true-positive rate of 1.0 and a false-positive rate of 0.015 in the authors' email-assistant testbed, including out-of-distribution worm variants.
